author: nadgruaz
body:
* **PTHR ID & PTN node:**
*DR PANTHER=PTHR11358; ARGINASE/AGMATINASE; 1
DR PANTHER=PTHR11358:SF26; GUANIDINO ACID HYDROLASE, MITOCHONDRIAL; 1
DR PAN-GO=Q9BSE5; 2 GO annotations based on evolutionary models


* **Sequences with problematic annotation (ID + gene/protein name):**
* ID GDAH_HUMAN; Reviewed [arginase]
AC Q9BSE5, Q5TDH1, Q9H5J3
GN Name=AGMAT;

* **Type of Issue: Erroneous source or erroneous propagation, or other issue**
* DR GO=GO:0008783; F:agmatinase activity; {IBA:GO_Central} 
* Could you delete this IBA annotation.
  Not a agmatinase

Initially proposed to function as agmatinase but this activity was not proved when using the purified enzyme. A recent study showed that it rather functions as a guanidino acid hydrolase. {*NA} **{}

RX PubMed=36543883; DOI=10.1038/s41598-022-26655-4
RA Sinn M., Stanoppi M., Hauth F., Fleming J.R., Funck D., Mayans O., Hartig J.S.
RT Guanidino acid hydrolysis by the human enzyme annotated as agmatinase.
RL journal article: Sci. Rep. 12:22088-22088 (2022)
 
* Add the label 'high priority' if needed. Generally high priority issues affect a lot of proteins, and annotations are incorrect (as opposed to just imprecise).

Many thanks in advance 
Nadine
title: PAINT issue: Not a agmatinase

author: marcfeuermann
body:
Hi Nadine,
Thanks for reporting this. The annotation has been removed and replaced in several nodes within this complex family, full of predicted horizontal transfers.
